source.original_text:
Construct a finite-dimensional Euclidean process from scalar completed Itô rows with almost surely continuous drift paths. Every slice up to the horizon is measurable, and almost every vector path is continuous on the horizon.

The positive horizon is T. The sample measure is finite, the filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and the driving standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The finite coordinate rows have progressive product-square-integrable diffusion coefficients. Their drift evaluations at each fixed time t≤T are almost-everywhere strongly measurable.
Each drift coordinate is continuous on [0,T] almost surely.

X_t^i=A_i(t)+\sum_j\int_0^t\eta_{ij}(s)\,dB^j_s.\qquad X_t:\Omega\to\mathbb R^I\text{ measurable for each }t\le T,\quad X_\cdot(\omega)\text{ continuous on }[0,T]\text{ a.e.}

lean.statement:
theorem anonymous_target.{u_1,
    u_2, u_3}
  {Ω : Type u_1} {I : Type u_2} {J : Type u_3} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
  {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal inferInstance} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : NNReal} {B : NNReal → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ J}
  (hB :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.BrownianMotion.IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B
      filtration μ)
  (hT : 0 < T)
  (hUsual : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration μ)
  (η :
    I → J → AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T)
  (A : I → NNReal → Ω → ℝ) (hAmeas : ∀ (i : I), ∀ t ≤ T, MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (A i t) μ)
  (hA : ∀ (i : I), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A i t ω) (Set.Icc 0 T)) :
  have X := fun t ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 fun i =>
      A i t ω +
        ∑ j,
          AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hT ⋯
            hUsual t ω;
  (∀ t ≤ T, Measurable (X t)) ∧ ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => X t ω) (Set.Icc 0 T)

blind_reconstruction.text:
Objects: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t. Define X(t,omega)=(A_i(t,omega)+sum_j I_T^j(eta_ij)(t,omega))_{i in I}. The integrand's toLp operation is its L^2 equivalence class represented by (omega,t)->eta(t,omega).

Domains: Omega measurable; I,J finite, with decidable equality required for J only; mu finite; filtration on R_+; T>0; B:R_+ x Omega->R^J; eta:I x J->ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T); A:I x R_+ x Omega->R; X takes values in Euclidean R^I.

Quantifiers: Universally spaces and instances,filtration,mu,T,B; Brownian,positive-T,usual hypotheses; eta,A; then for every i and t<=T the measurability hypothesis, and for every i an a.e. continuity hypothesis. Conclusion: every t<=T has measurable X_t, and almost every omega has a continuous X-path on [0,T].

Assumptions: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). For all i and t<=T, A_i(t,.) is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. For each i, mu-a.e. omega, A_i(.,omega) is continuous on [0,T]. Bounded variation and adaptedness of A are not required.

Conclusion: For every t<=T, X(t,.) is measurable (the conclusion says Measurable, not merely almost-everywhere measurable); and for mu-a.e. omega, t->X(t,omega) is continuous on [0,T].

Scopes: Slice measurability is pointwise in time. The finite collection of a.e. coordinate continuity assumptions yields the asserted one a.e. event for the vector path. All claims are restricted to [0,T].

Constant dependencies: No existential constant is stated; X depends on A,eta,the completed Ito choices,B,T and the ambient data.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.EuclideanBrownianCoordinates
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoEuclideanRowRegularity

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped BigOperators NNReal
open BrownianMotion ProgressiveL2 EuclideanBrownianCoordinates ItoIntegralProcess

/-- Actual completed coordinate rows with continuous drifts have measurable
vector slices and almost surely continuous vector paths on the horizon. -/
theorem measurable_continuousOn_euclidean_ito_rows
    {Ω I J : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)}
    {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : ℝ≥0}
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ J}
    (hB : IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration μ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration μ)
    (η : I → J → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T) (A : I → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ)
    (hAmeas : ∀ i t, t ≤ T → AEStronglyMeasurable (A i t) μ)
    (hA : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A i t ω) (Icc 0 T)) :
    let X := fun (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : I => A i t ω + ∑ j : J,
      itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual t ω)
    (∀ t ≤ T, Measurable (X t)) ∧ (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => X t ω) (Icc 0 T)) := by
  intro X
  let M (i : I) (j : J) := itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual
  let _ : μ.IsComplete := Measure.isComplete_iff.2
    (fun s hs => filtration.le 0 _ (hUsual.completeAt 0 s hs))
  constructor
  · intro t ht
    have hM (i : I) : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ω => ∑ j : J, M i j t ω) μ :=
      (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ fun j _ =>
        (((itoIntegralProcess_stronglyAdapted (η i j) hT
          ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual) t).mono
            (filtration.le t)).aestronglyMeasurable).congr
        (Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [Finset.sum_apply, M])
    have hRow (i : I) : Measurable (fun ω => A i t ω + ∑ j : J, M i j t ω) :=
      ((hAmeas i t ht).add (hM i)).aemeasurable.nullMeasurable.measurable_of_complete
    exact (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (I → ℝ)).measurable.comp (measurable_pi_lambda _ hRow)
  · filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 hA] with ω hω
    have hRow (i : I) : ContinuousOn (fun t => A i t ω + ∑ j : J, M i j t ω) (Icc 0 T) :=
      (hω i).add (continuousOn_finsetSum _ fun j _ =>
        itoIntegralProcess_continuousOn (η i j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual ω)
    exact (PiLp.continuous_toLp 2 (fun _ : I => ℝ)).comp_continuousOn (continuousOn_pi.2 hRow)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoEuclideanRowRegularity

steps.title: Assemble measurable slices
steps.text: Strong adaptation gives measurable slices of each completed integral. A finite sum with the drift is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Completeness from the usual conditions gives ordinary measurability of that slice.
steps.lean:
intro X
  let M (i : I) (j : J) := itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual
  let _ : μ.IsComplete := Measure.isComplete_iff.2
    (fun s hs => filtration.le 0 _ (hUsual.completeAt 0 s hs))
  constructor
  · intro t ht
    have hM (i : I) : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ω => ∑ j : J, M i j t ω) μ :=
      (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ fun j _ =>
        (((itoIntegralProcess_stronglyAdapted (η i j) hT
          ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual) t).mono
            (filtration.le t)).aestronglyMeasurable).congr
        (Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [Finset.sum_apply, M])
    have hRow (i : I) : Measurable (fun ω => A i t ω + ∑ j : J, M i j t ω) :=
      ((hAmeas i t ht).add (hM i)).aemeasurable.nullMeasurable.measurable_of_complete
    exact (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (I → ℝ)).measurable.comp (measurable_pi_lambda _ hRow)

steps.title: Assemble continuous paths
steps.text: The completed integrals have continuous paths on the horizon. Intersect the finitely many drift continuity events and use continuity of each coordinate to get continuity in the Euclidean topology.
steps.formula: \bigl(\forall i,\ X_\cdot^i(\omega)\text{ continuous on }[0,T]\bigr)\Longrightarrow X_\cdot(\omega)\text{ continuous on }[0,T].
steps.lean:
· filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 hA] with ω hω
    have hRow (i : I) : ContinuousOn (fun t => A i t ω + ∑ j : J, M i j t ω) (Icc 0 T) :=
      (hω i).add (continuousOn_finsetSum _ fun j _ =>
        itoIntegralProcess_continuousOn (η i j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual ω)
    exact (PiLp.continuous_toLp 2 (fun _ : I => ℝ)).comp_continuousOn (continuousOn_pi.2 hRow)
